title: Absorbed, Not Credited?
description: What visible citations can—and cannot—tell us about AI answers to shopping questions.

sections.heading: Some answers gave no visible credit
sections.body: Four answers to the two general prompts in ChatGPT and AI Mode contained no visible citations. That observation describes the interface; it does not reveal how the answer was produced.

sections.heading: Specific questions changed the citation pattern
sections.body: Price, location and current-information prompts showed citations in all three sampled tools. For the value-for-money prompt, eight of fourteen links pointed to independent reviewers.

sections.heading: Keep inference separate from observation
sections.body: The title raises a question. An uncited answer does not prove training-data absorption, identify an uncredited source, or establish whether retrieval occurred. I would use the findings to design repeated citation tests, not to estimate lost traffic.

methodology: Six prompts compared across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode and AI Overviews on 24 October 2026 in Vancouver. The report records eighteen answers and fifty-three credited sources.
limitations: Visible citations are an incomplete view of a system’s internal process. The original PDF contains interpretations that should be read with this distinction in mind. No browsing traces, training data, traffic or conversion data were available.
